body:
`ITouch::config_t::freq` defaulted to 1 MHz. I2C touch drivers that do not set a clock in their constructor therefore ran the bus at 1 MHz unless the user's configuration set `cfg.freq`:

CST816S, CST226, CST3530, CST9217, GT911, CHSC6x, CHSC6540, NS2009, TT21xxx, GSLx680

Most touch controllers are on I2C, and Fast-mode (400 kHz) is the common upper limit in their datasheets, so the default is now 400 kHz.

### What changes

- I2C touch drivers above, when the configuration does not set `cfg.freq`: 1 MHz → 400 kHz.
- SPI touch drivers (XPT2046, RA8875, STMPE610) set 1 MHz in their constructors and keep it when the configuration is read with `config()` and modified.
- **Behavior change:** code that passes a newly constructed `config_t` to `config()` without setting `cfg.freq` now gets 400 kHz on the SPI touch drivers too. Set `cfg.freq` to keep 1 MHz.
- Configurations that set `cfg.freq` are unchanged. FT5x06 already set 400 kHz.
- Boards set up by the board detection are unchanged: every detected I2C touch is given its clock explicitly (400 kHz unless the board sets another).

### Side effects

- With a software I2C port, the bit-banged clock now inserts the half-period wait it skipped at 1 MHz, so each touch read takes longer.
- GSLx680: its firmware download in `init()` takes about 0.4 s longer.

### Checks

- Built for the CI targets (Arduino and ESP-IDF versions); no new warnings. Host tests pass.
- Fork CI passed (no new warnings).
title: touch: make the default touch I2C clock 400 kHz
